| stats count as id | eval id="11-22" | eval id=split( id, "-" ) | mvexpand id | makecontinuous id span=1 | regex id="^(.*)\1$",

As with the previous version we'll use regular expressions to select the correct IDs.,5,AdventOfCode25 Day 2 alt<-O->part 1
Unfortunately this errors (notice the red triangle 🔺).

The makecontinuous command is trying to make the smallest ID from the lowest range continuous with the highest ID from the highest range. We need to keep each ranges separate.",6,AdventOfCode25 Day 2 alt<-O->part 1

| stats count as id_range | eval id_range=split( "11-22,95-115,998-1012,1188511880-1188511890,222220-222224,1698522-1698528,446443-446449,38593856-38593862,565653-565659,824824821-824824827,2121212118-2121212124", "," ) | mvexpand id_range | map [| stats count as id | eval id="$id_range$" | eval id=split( id, "-" ) | mvexpand id | makecontinuous id span=1 | regex id="^(.*)\1$" ] maxsearches=100,"

The map command allows to run a new search for each search result.
Note how each search can refer to the search result it came from with tokens between dollar signs.
Warning: because it starts a whole new search for each result, map will not scale terribly well. It is limited to 10 by default, though you can increase the limit with the maxsearches option.
